title: "How do our free variables compare to their limits?"
---


::: {#5b9435b5 .cell execution_count=2}
``` {.python .cell-code}
opt = optimise(static_margin=0.10)

# Two readings, because "free" is not one question. Distance to the bound says
# whether a bound binds now; re-solving with the box widened says whether it is
# shaping the answer, which a variable can suffer from while sitting well inside
# its own limits. Widened toward physically meaningful values only -- scaling
# each box by a fixed fraction drove the aspect-ratio floor negative, and the
# NaN geometry that followed read as though the bound had been helping.
WIDER = dict(aspect_ratio=(1.2, 20.0), tail_arm_chords=(0.8, 14.0),
             h_tail_ratio=(0.03, 0.70), h_tail_incidence=(-12.0, 6.0))

rows = []
for k, (lo, hi) in DESIGN_BOUNDS.items():
    v = opt[k]
    _saved = DESIGN_BOUNDS[k]
    DESIGN_BOUNDS[k] = WIDER[k]
    try:
        widened = optimise(static_margin=0.10)["sink"]
    finally:
        DESIGN_BOUNDS[k] = _saved
    rows.append(dict(name=k.replace("_", " "), lo=lo, hi=hi, v=v,
                     frac=(v - lo) / (hi - lo),
                     near=min(v - lo, hi - v) / (hi - lo),
                     gain=widened / opt["sink"] - 1))

tightest = min(rows, key=lambda r: r["near"])
worst_gain = max(abs(r["gain"]) for r in rows)
alpha_headroom = (9.0 - opt["alpha"]) / 11.0

# The claim of the entry: nothing binds, and nothing is being shaped by a bound.
assert all(r["near"] > 0.01 for r in rows)
assert worst_gain < 1e-4
```
:::


**Answer.** All four sit inside their limits, and widening any one box changes
the sink rate by under 1e\-06 — so no bound
is shaping this design (@fig-bounds). The closest is
**tail arm chords** at [2\.2%]{.key}
of its range from the floor. Trim angle is the real constraint to watch, sitting
1\.3° below the stall cap.

::: {.callout-warning}
## The first version of this test was wrong
It reported the aspect-ratio bound as helpful. That was a zero-lift dive, not a glider.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Assumed

1. **Widened boxes** stay physically meaningful, not merely wider.
2. **One start per solve**; the surface has several basins.
:::

    ax.text(-0.03, yi, f"{lo:g}", ha="right", va="center", fontsize=7, color="0.4")
    ax.text(1.03, yi, f"{hi:g}", ha="left", va="center", fontsize=7, color="0.4")
ax.set_yticks(y, labels)
ax.set_xlim(-0.14, 1.14)

ax.invert_yaxis()
for s in ["top", "right", "left"]:
    ax.spines[s].set_visible(False)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
